items.headline: Canada and Germany commit up to $300M to Bengio's LawZero for safe AI research
items.summary: The Canadian and German governments announced joint backing (CAD 150M and EUR 100M) for Yoshua Bengio's Montreal non-profit LawZero, funding a new Berlin office and sovereign compute partnership aimed at building safe-by-design AI systems as an alternative to frontier labs racing on capability.

items.headline: Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman attacks Anthropic's Claude 'model welfare' approach
items.summary: In an essay titled 'A warning about model welfare,' Suleyman argued that Anthropic's constitution for Claude, which treats the model's possible consciousness as an open question, is circular reasoning and anthropomorphization that could make advanced AI harder to control — a rare public rift between two frontier labs over AI philosophy.

items.headline: Anthropic and OpenAI move to embed independent safety evaluators inside their labs
items.summary: Following Dario Amodei's 'We Must Pace the Frontier' essay calling for a deliberate slowdown in frontier AI development, both Anthropic and Sam Altman's OpenAI said they would give third-party evaluators such as METR and Redwood Research permanent, employee-level access to report safety findings publicly.

items.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang breaks with Anthropic and OpenAI CEOs over AI safety pacing
items.summary: At Salesforce's Dreamforce conference, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang publicly diverged from Dario Amodei and Sam Altman on how urgently the industry needs to slow down, underscoring a widening rift between chipmakers pushing for scale and lab leaders newly emphasizing caution.

items.headline: Google launches Gemini 3.8 Live, undercutting OpenAI's GPT-Live-1 on price
items.summary: Google's new full-duplex voice model sustains conversation across 97 languages and runs tool calls mid-speech, priced at about $1.38/hour versus roughly $3+/hour for OpenAI's rival GPT-Live-1, intensifying price competition in real-time voice AI.

items.headline: Apple ships iOS 27 with Google Gemini-powered Siri
items.summary: Apple's new Siri, built on a custom-tuned variant of Google's Gemini model, rolled out with iOS 27, adding multi-turn conversational memory and handling complex queries that exceed Apple's on-device models — a major shift after Apple's earlier in-house Siri overhaul struggled.

items.headline: Google lets AI agents control Google Home smart-home devices
items.summary: Google extended agentic capabilities to Google Home, allowing AI agents to directly operate connected smart-home hardware, part of a broader industry push to move AI agents from chat interfaces into physical/IoT control.

items.headline: Z.ai raises roughly $5 billion in second major fundraise in two months
items.summary: Chinese AI developer Z.ai (Zhipu) completed a combined share placement and convertible bond sale worth about $5 billion to fund next-generation GLM foundation models and large-scale compute infrastructure, highlighting the intensity of China's domestic AI funding race.

items.headline: Palantir, Nvidia and Booz Allen restrict use of Anthropic's Claude over data-retention concerns
items.summary: Several major enterprise and government-adjacent customers are reportedly limiting use of Anthropic's Fable model for sensitive work, demanding stronger zero-data-retention guarantees before broader deployment, a sign of growing enterprise scrutiny of frontier-model data handling.

items.headline: Shanghai AI Lab quietly open-sources Atria, a 744B-parameter agent model
items.summary: Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory released Atria under an MIT license on Hugging Face, with BF16 and FP8 checkpoints claiming a 92.5 score on the BrowseComp web-browsing benchmark, pushing the frontier of open-weight agentic models forward.

items.headline: ByteDance's Zhang Yiming becomes Asia's richest person
items.summary: ByteDance founder Zhang Yiming overtook Gautam Adani to become Asia's wealthiest individual at roughly $105 billion, driven by the company's TikTok US joint venture with Oracle and Silver Lake and its Doubao chatbot surpassing 75 million monthly active users.

items.headline: Trump-Nvidia camp and Anthropic-OpenAI camp split publicly over AI regulation
items.summary: A regulatory divide crystallized this week, with President Trump, Nvidia's Jensen Huang and former White House crypto czar David Sacks on one side favoring minimal restrictions, against Anthropic's Dario Amodei, OpenAI's Sam Altman and Elon Musk pushing for coordinated safety oversight.
